stage_vocabulary.SPEC: Reverified and specced in its WI doc. Nothing run.
stage_vocabulary.MEASURED: Fix applied and its acceptance numbers exist; the orchestrator has not yet re-run the doc's definition of done.
stage_vocabulary.LANDED: Definition of done re-run by the orchestrator and passing, in the working tree. Committing or publishing is the user's call and is not part of the stage.
stage_vocabulary.BLOCKED: Waiting on an open decision, or on a dependency that has hit a problem. Plain unmet dependencies are not BLOCKED - dependency order already handles those.
stage_vocabulary.CLOSED: Terminal, with reason recorded (won't fix / superseded). Do not re-open without new evidence named in the reason.

model_vocabulary.fable-5.1: claude-fable-5-1. Novel statistical construction where a wrong derivation is expensive and hard to detect from the output - estimators, identification arguments, inference machinery. Reach for it when the failure mode is a plausible-looking number, not an error.
model_vocabulary.opus-5: claude-opus-5. The default. Anything that makes a ruling, designs an aggregation, moves the feature contract, or turns a measurement into a claim.
model_vocabulary.sonnet-5: claude-sonnet-5. The method is already written down and the judgment call is made - ingest, enumeration, a named refit, a declared schema note. Step back up to opus-5 the moment the leaf doc leaves a choice open.
model_vocabulary.haiku-4-5: claude-haiku-4-5. Throughput work with a mechanical check on the output. Nothing in the tree currently qualifies: every live item either writes into the contract, rules on leakage, or produces a claim.

decisions.question: Gate A definition: does a lapped car ahead make a sample invalid always, or only within 3 s?
decisions.context: Literal reading (design note line 21) gives 88.6% valid, below the 90% gate. A 3 s reading gives 97.0%, passing in every season. DA-01 evidence: _roadmap/_dirty-air/_evidence/DA-01-2026-10-23/NOTE.md.
decisions.recommendation: Lapped car ahead invalidates a sample only within 3 s. Beyond 3 s the sample is in the reference band.
decisions.resolution: Owner accepted the 3 s reading. Design note line 21 amended to match on 2026-10-23. Gate A under this rule: 97.0% overall, 95.5-98.5% per season (PASS).

decisions.question: Proceed without new F1 timing data for now, and carry the known gaps as exceptions?
decisions.context: F1 livetiming needs an F1 TV login since October 2026. Bronze holds 2018-2025 except the 2018 gaps (Australia and Bahrain telemetry, China and Germany track status before lap ~30). Marshal-sector maps are not in bronze. OpenF1 covers 2023+ only. Owner intends a private, non-commercial project for portfolio and friends.
decisions.recommendation: Proceed on bronze. Record the 2018 gaps and missing marshal maps as exceptions. Get the data before the ML step.
decisions.resolution: Owner: proceed without the data for now, close the rest, and treat these as exceptions. New data (FastF1 with F1 TV, marshal sectors) comes before the ML step. Private use only; F1 terms are personal, non-commercial.

decisions.question: Micro-sector grain and user display: seconds or metres, and is metres shown to users?

Intuition review (_roadmap/_dirty-air/_evidence/INTUITION-2026-10-23/NOTE.md) recommended seconds only for labels. Existing lap-map page computes gap as distance divided by speed, which DA-01 found biased above 1 s.
decisions.recommendation: Seconds only for the analysis and for every label. Metres at most a methods-page check later. Fix the lap-map gap to the seconds method.
decisions.resolution: Owner: seconds only. Fix the lap-map gap calculation. Metres label not built now.

decisions.question: Micro-sectors per lap: how many?
decisions.context: Options 10 to 20 per lap. About 300 samples per lap in 2018-19 and about 400 in 2020-21. Rule of thumb is 10 to 15 samples per slice, which caps the count near 20 to 30. 20 matches the marshal-sector grid, which DA-03 needs to rule out local yellows. Samples per slice not yet measured.
decisions.recommendation: 20 per lap, fixed for every circuit. Pre-register 10 as a sensitivity check under the same no-rescue rule as metres.
decisions.resolution: Owner: 20 per lap. Pre-register 10 as the sensitivity check. DA-02 must measure samples per slice before the count is frozen; drop to 15 only on that evidence.

decisions.question: DA-03 pre-registration amendment: corner thresholds, P3 exceptions, P3 pass rule, DRS rule, commit order, Path A or B.
decisions.context: Owner review of the DA-02P draft (wi/DA-03-preregistration-amendment-draft.md), 2026-10-25. Naming ruling recorded in the transform log D11: v16 is the TRANSFORM label version, v17 is the ML model. 2026-10-25 update: thresholds ruled; flat-out kinks split to DD10, since resolved (split into a flat class, 280 km/h). Path A or B (DD2): owner selected B, gated on DA-03 and DA-04.
decisions.recommendation: Accept the exceptions, the P3 pass rule, the DRS rule, the commit order and fixed corner cut-offs of 120 and 200 km/h as drafted. Flat-out kinks are split out to DD10.
decisions.resolution: Owner 2026-10-25. (1) Corner thresholds ACCEPTED (owner 2026-10-25, 'okay perf', accepting the recommendation): fixed cut-offs of 120 and 200 km/h for every track, 100 m and 150 m straight buffers, apex-speed definition as drafted. Basis: the corner analysis in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-justin-github-off-the-pace/4688e87f-3ff1-4470-87f4-4afc2bd5deef/scratchpad/corners/ (breaks_out.txt for the pooled and per-season distribution checks, options_out.txt for the fixed, pooled and per-track options). 200 km/h matches a dip in the pooled apex-speed distribution that holds across seasons; 120 km/h is a physics choice (about a third of the downforce of 200 km/h). (2) Exceptions ACCEPTED: 2020 Tuscan and 2020 Sakhir have no corner data and drop out of the fast-corner test (p3 only); 2021 Belgium borrows corner speeds from 2022. (3) P3 pass rule ACCEPTED: (a) fast-corner loss positive with 95% CI excluding 0; (b) fast minus straight positive with CI excluding 0; (c) straight effect at or below 0; required pooled and in each era 2018-21 and 2022-25. (4) DRS rule ACCEPTED: drop micro-sectors where DRS is open at entry or exit, and drop unknown; the DRS-closed result is reported as secondary and cannot rescue a failed main result. (5) Commit order ACCEPTED: model and test edits first, then the pre-registration alone. (6) Path A or B: owner selected B on 2026-10-25 (DD2), gated on DA-03 and DA-04; no label moves until both pass. The flat-out kink question was recorded separately as DD10 and resolved 2026-10-25: split into a flat class. DD9 is RESOLVED on its other items.

decisions.question: Flat-out kinks in the fast-corner class: keep them in the high class as drafted, or split them into their own class before the fit? Blocks DA-03 and the hash of the pre-registration amendment.
decisions.context: Corner analysis (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-justin-github-off-the-pace/4688e87f-3ff1-4470-87f4-4afc2bd5deef/scratchpad/corners/, options_out.txt, fixed 120/200 option): 205 of 869 high-corner race entries (24%) have an apex speed of 280 km/h or more. These are flat-out kinks where a following car may get a tow, which could weaken the fast-corner test P3(a) and (b) by mixing tow gain into the high class. Not answered by the owner when the thresholds were accepted (DD9).
options: (a) Keep flat kinks in the fast (high) class as drafted: no map change, the high class stays 200 km/h and above.
(b) Split kinks at 280 km/h or more into their own class before the fit: changes the map, the P3 spec and the pass rule text, and must be done before the hash. CHOSEN by owner 2026-10-25.
decisions.resolution: Owner 2026-10-25: B. Split flat-out kinks into their own class before the fit. Class rule: "flat: apex speed at or above 280 km/h, not a straight". The 280 km/h number is taken from the corner analysis (205 of 869 high-corner race entries) and is TO BE CONFIRMED in the amendment text before commit. Classes are now low, medium, high, flat, straight, link, mixed, no_geometry. In the P3 test, flat is excluded from the high-speed effect and reported separately; high means 200 km/h and above and below 280 km/h. The P3 pass rule (a) to (c) is restated for high without flat in the amendment draft; that restated wording is NEW and the owner has not yet read it. The map (int_microsector_corner_class), the p3 spec and the row-count table must be changed to match before the hash; model SQL was not touched in this step.

watch_vocabulary.ship-blocker: Publishing or shipping without this breaks something users see. `board.py --ship` exits 1 while one is open.
watch_vocabulary.hazard: A standing trap that damages tracked files or results if someone does the obvious thing. Read before running anything nearby.
watch_vocabulary.uncommitted: Verified work that lives only in the working tree. Committing is the user's call.
watch_vocabulary.unreviewed: Changes in the working tree that no orchestrator has read or tested. Not to be built on until reviewed.
watch_vocabulary.unverified: A claim or code path that was run in one place only (dev but not CI, agent report but not re-run).
watch_vocabulary.stale-artifact: A built or generated thing that no longer matches the source it came from until it is rebuilt.
watch_vocabulary.pending-ruling: A question for the human that is not (yet) a blocking FD: it changes a note, a value or a scope, not an item's ability to run.
watch_vocabulary.gate-gap: A guard that does not guard: it errors, skips files silently, or cannot fail.
watch_vocabulary.debt: Known, documented, deliberately left. Each needs an owner eventually.

watch_model_vocabulary.haiku: Maps to haiku-4-5. A binary check, or recording a resolution the evidence or the user has already settled: is it committed, did the named tests pass on the rebuild, write down the accept. The output has a mechanical check (a test result, a file list, git log).
watch_model_vocabulary.sonnet: Maps to sonnet-5. The fix or the options are written down in the rule: pick between two named options, run a named rebuild or export and check the pages, review a diff, reconcile counts, reword text to a meaning already settled.
watch_model_vocabulary.opus: Maps to opus-5 (fable-5.1 if the rule turns into a new estimator). Rules on a trade-off, designs the fix, audits a decision, or turns a measurement into a claim: label-moving changes, leakage boundaries, gate runs before a promotion.

watch_rules.title: IsAccurate may drop 2018 race laps for a reason unrelated to the lap
watch_rules.detail: is_valid_lap requires is_accurate, which is FastF1's start/end sync flag, not a lap-time check. The repo's qualifying audit found 2018 leaves it unset for about 26% of timed laps (under 0.4% in other seasons). The race audit has not been split by season. If 2018 races drop valid laps the same way, the cliff and dirty-air samples for 2018 are thinner than the other seasons, and the 2018 numbers should be read with that caveat.
watch_rules.clears_when: Split the is_accurate false share by season for race laps, and record whether 2018 is an outlier. Then decide whether to keep the gate for 2018 or flag it.
